title: Jude and the Salt
premise: Felix Fairweather fled her hedge-witch master years ago and now keeps meticulous ledgers for the Guild of Improbable Trade, where souls, names, and years are bought and sold. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Felix recognizes the tongue from her master's forbidden books—and learns the child is a soul the Guild itself sold to the court beneath the mountain, with Felix's own name on the receipt. To steal the soul back, she must return to the master she betrayed, trade pieces of her own memory as currency, and confront the truth that she once sold something of her own to survive. In the salt courts below, Felix discovers she cannot rescue the child without unmaking the false identity she built, and she chooses to give up her stolen years so the child can live whole—returning to the surface nameless, but finally free.
about_author: Kestrel Villalobos grew up in a coastal town where the tide charts were kept by three generations of her family, and she still swears the sea keeps accounts of its own. She writes fantasy about bargains, bookkeeping, and the people who fall between the lines.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She catalogs the Guild's strangest inventory—a bottled lullaby, a debt of shadows—establishing her precision and her careful invisibility. A senior trader hints that auditors are coming. Emotional beat: the comfort of order, and the first crack of unease.

chapters.title: A Knock in Old Tongue
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A child appears at the Guild's door at closing, speaking a language no living person should know. Felix alone recognizes fragments from her master's banned books and hides the child in the ledger room before the Guild can 'appraise' her. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into protectiveness.

chapters.title: What the Receipt Said
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Digging through sealed ledgers, Felix finds the sale record: the child's soul, sold to the court beneath the mountain—signed with her own apprentice mark from years ago, a signature she doesn't remember making. Emotional beat: horror and self-doubt entwined.

chapters.title: Salt on the Windowsill
chapters.summary: The child's POV, rendered as impressionistic fragments. She remembers the mountain, a court of salt, and a woman's voice reading numbers aloud. She draws Felix's face from memory. Emotional beat: eerie recognition that their fates are braided.

chapters.title: The Guild Takes Notice
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The Guild discovers the missing entry and suspects Felix of theft. Her mentor-figure, the trader Marrow, covers for her—but the price is a favor owed. Emotional beat: the cost of allies in a world of transactions.

chapters.title: Road Toward the Hedge
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix flees with the child toward her old master's cottage, pursued by a Guild appraiser. On the road, the child's presence erodes Felix's carefully maintained anonymity. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness growing between them.

chapters.title: The Master's Garden
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Reunion with Odile the hedge-witch, who is neither forgiving nor surprised. Odile confirms the old tongue is the language of the mountain court—and that Felix studied it once, before she sold the memory. Emotional beat: shame, and the first hint that Felix's past is not what she believes.

chapters.title: Memory as Currency
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Odile explains the trade: the mountain court accepts memories as tender. To enter and bargain, Felix must spend recollections—and she has already spent more than she knows. Emotional beat: dread that identity itself is finite.

chapters.title: The Appraiser's Offer
chapters.summary: The appraiser Vess's POV. Vess catches up to them and offers Felix immunity if she surrenders the child as Guild property. Vess is not cruel, merely procedural, which makes it worse. Emotional beat: the seductive reasonableness of betrayal.

chapters.title: What Felix Sold
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Odile performs a risky rite to return one of Felix's purchased-back memories: Felix, starving and sixteen, trading a year of her life to a salt-merchant to survive the winter—the first transaction in a chain. Emotional beat: grief for the girl she was, compassion replacing self-contempt.

chapters.title: Descent at the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Leaving the child hidden with Odile, Felix descends through the salt gate with Marrow's favor token and Vess shadowing her. The mountain tastes of brine and old promises. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into courage.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The mountain court: nobles of crystallized memory who speak in the old tongue and remember everything, including Felix's first sale. They offer her a seat, permanence, safety. Emotional beat: temptation of forgetting versus the ache of being known.

chapters.title: The Child's True Name
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The child begins speaking, and Odile realizes she is not a random victim—she is the last speaker of the old tongue, the court's living archive, sold to the Guild by someone inside it. Emotional beat: the scale of the conspiracy revealed.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Brine
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix negotiates with the Salt Regent: the child's soul for memories of her choosing. The Regent, amused, demands the memory of why Felix ran from Odile—a memory Felix has never been able to retrieve. Emotional beat: terror of what she might learn.

chapters.title: The Memory Returned
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She pays, and the truth floods back: Odile once tried to save Felix from the salt-merchant, and Felix, panicked, betrayed her—selling Odile's location to buy her own escape. The Guild's audit trail, her forged signature: all cover-ups by the merchant's network. Emotional beat: devastation, and the collapse of her self-forgiven story.

chapters.title: Vess Chooses
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Ordered to seize the child when she's brought below as 'collateral,' Vess reads the original contract and finds the Guild's seal forged by its own Grand Ledger. She burns her orders. Emotional beat: an instrument of the system breaking from it.

chapters.title: Theft of a Soul
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, with Vess. The heist: while the court debates Felix's seat among them, Vess swaps the ledger entry and Felix carries the child's soul—a small salt-white flame—out through the memory vaults. Emotional beat: breathless, triumphant defiance.

chapters.title: The Regent's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The court seals the mountain; no one leaves with a stolen flame unless a debt of equal weight is paid. Felix offers the years she bought with her first sale—the remainder of her own stolen time. Emotional beat: the price of survival, finally paid forward.

chapters.title: Ascension
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, fading. She and Vess climb out as Felix's memories thin like morning fog. The child, restored, speaks Felix's name in the old tongue—making it a gift rather than a record. Emotional beat: bittersweet release.

chapters.title: The Garden in Spring
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The child, whole, lives with Odile; Vess takes a post auditing the Guild from within. Felix returns with gaps in her mind and no ledger of her own. Emotional beat: quiet homecoming, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: What Felix Keeps
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Some things survived the payment: the smell of ink, the child's laughter, an unexplained tenderness toward Odile. Felix begins a new ledger with a single entry—not a debt, but a gift given. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt from choice rather than survival.

chapters.title: The Salt Remembers
chapters.summary: The child's POV, closing frame. Now the last speaker of the old tongue, she teaches Felix its first word—her own name, Fairweather, which means one who carries storms lightly. Far below, the salt court keeps its books, and one line reads: paid in full. Emotional beat: peace, memory honored, the future open.
